biography: Pedro Gomes, a name whispered with respect and a hint of exasperation in the Opala Old Stock Race paddock, hails from the vibrant heart of São Paulo. His racing journey began not on asphalt, but on the dusty dirt tracks of his grandfather's farm, where he learned to coax every ounce of performance from a battered old Willys Jeep. It wasn't until his late twenties that he traded the farm for the track, after a local mechanic, impressed by Gomes's uncanny ability to diagnose engine problems by ear, sponsored his entry into a regional Opala series. Gomes quickly proved a natural, his defensive style frustrating rivals and captivating fans. His defining moment came in 2018 at Interlagos, when he held off a charging pack of veterans for the final ten laps, securing his first major victory. Now, at 37, Gomes is considered to be at the peak of his prowess, a wily veteran known for his tactical brilliance and unwavering resolve.
drivingStyle: Gomes is a master of defensive driving, a calculated strategist who prioritizes consistency and tire conservation. He rarely makes flashy overtakes, preferring to pressure opponents into mistakes. His cornering style is smooth and precise, maximizing exit speed rather than risking it all on late braking. Under pressure, Gomes remains remarkably composed, a testament to his years of experience. He's known for his meticulous pre-race preparation, studying track maps and analyzing opponent tendencies to gain any possible advantage.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2020 Opala Old Stock Race Championship after a season-long battle with Ricardo Vargas, securing the title by a single point in the final race at Curitiba.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at Goiânia in 2017 due to a mechanical failure, costing him a potential victory and severely damaging his championship hopes.
